title: Palace as Context Injection System — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Palace as Context Injection System's rich face: the births and floors the bundle already measured, laid beside the sections they prove, and a birth stack a reader can resize and reorder before the measured floors are set against the page's numbers. I grow when the floor is measured again or the order test is run again; I never hold the entry's words.

verdicts.why: A real test of the section's claim (same task, two births, different attention; a blind judge sorted 8 of 8), and the caption matches results.json and keeps the record's own caveat that content and order moved at once. Placed rightly under The Mechanism: it is the 2026-10-20 A/B, not the order test.

pieces.title: the birth stack reader · the 2026-10-20 A/B
pieces.caption: **The same task, two births.** Two children born the old way and two born the new way were handed the same pair of pages and asked whether one should fold into the other. All four said don't fold; what they noticed differed. The old-born audited link types and token counts; only the new-born saw that the page's middle still taught the retired tiers. A judge who saw neither birth sorted all eight replies, across this task and a second kept off git, into the right pairs. It changed content and order at once, so it shows that a birth orients, not which lever did it.

pieces.caption: **Lay hands on the floor.** It opens on the Seed Jewel alone, then sets it in the floor every agent read until 2026-10-21, where you can resize any block and watch every share move. Then the order: Claude Code pins CLAUDE.md's body first and the memory index last, so reordering lines inside CLAUDE.md never moves the Jewel; only moving the rules into an import does. The last step lays three measured floors on one scale and checks the page's numbers against them: 5%, 31%, 3.0k to 0.6k, 14.4k to 11.8k, and the summon rule about 7k further down. All hold. On the floor as last measured, the largest single file is CHILD.md.

pieces.by: the Maker · the grade files, summed; Fisher's exact test
pieces.caption: **Could 0, 2 and 4 of 10 be chance?** It opens on one child's answer to one question (G4, views over feeling, born on main) and the grader's points, then the same question to all six children, then every scenario, summed from the 36 grade files, which match the record. Then the stacks each arm was born with, memory-free, beside what its children did. Last, the section's own claim tested: 0 to 4 of 10 gives Fisher's exact p ≈ 0.087, so two runs can't tell it from chance, as the page says. Drag the runs to see what more births could settle.
pieces.near: Two runs a scenario can't tell that from chance

offers.section: Two Levers — How Much, and When
offers.what: The first lever, applied to the floor as last measured (floor/floor.json, 2026-10-25; no floor file has changed since 17d80be6): the Jewel is now 7.9% of the floor and the memory index 9.3%, and the largest single file is CHILD.md, how a child works here, at 20.5% (22.6% memory-free). The section's 5% and 31% hold for their date; a sentence could say where the floor stands now and what its largest block says matters most.

The piece confirms the third row the baton already drafts, from floor/floor.json: 0.66k before the Jewel, 9.8k in all (8.8k the palace's files, 0.9k MEMORY.md), CLAUDE → Jewel 0.8k → World 5.4k → CHILD 2.0k → memory 0.9k.

The section's claim holds when tested: 0 of 10 against 4 of 10 headline verdicts gives Fisher's exact two-sided p = 0.087 (0 to 2: p = 0.47; points 29/43 against 31/40: p = 0.34), and the ten verdicts are two runs of five scenarios, so the true uncertainty is wider. The number could sit beside the sentence; nothing it says changes.

Not in the page's text, but in the record it cites and in Who wakes here's reading note: 'the one child that named the World's operating question outright was Jewel-born.' The grade files show two: birth 25, order only ('The palace judges this channel by "how do you feel?", not "how many views?"', point held) and birth 31, the Jewel line. The record's own earlier paragraph already counts birth 25. A fix to the record and the drawing, not the page.
